name: olmOCR-bench
intro: olmOCR-Bench 以简单、无歧义、可机器核验的页面事实评估PDF线性化，而不是比较完整参考转录。论文v3从七类文档来源构建1,403份PDF与7,010项五类核心测试，并为每份PDF执行基线检查；固定HF快照含7,010项核心记录及9项显式基线覆盖。评测对八个来源组的通过率等权宏平均。
build_method: 七类来源专用采集，PII与公开传播意图联合过滤，URL级去污染，人工设计复核与GPT-4o辅助测试生成（温度0.1）
metric: 二元单元测试通过率；七类文档来源加baseline的八组等权宏平均；95%置信区间
eval_feature: 存在/缺失/阅读顺序/表格/公式五类核心测试, 每PDF基线, 字符串规范化, 论文10,000次Bootstrap
scale: 论文v3表与固定发布：1,403份PDF、7,010项核心测试；固定JSONL另含9项显式baseline
build_method_en: Seven source-specific acquisition pipelines, joint PII/public-dissemination-intent filtering, URL-level decontamination, manual design/review plus GPT-4o-assisted test generation (temperature 0.1)
eval_feature_en: Five core test families for presence, absence, order, tables, and formulas; one baseline per PDF; normalized strings; paper 10,000-sample bootstrap
intro_en: olmOCR-Bench evaluates PDF linearization with simple, unambiguous, machine-checkable page facts instead of a complete reference transcription. Paper v3 builds 1,403 PDFs and 7,010 core tests from seven document sources and applies a baseline check to every PDF. The fixed Hugging Face snapshot stores those 7,010 core records plus nine explicit baseline overrides. Evaluation equally macro-averages pass rates from the seven document-source groups and the baseline group.

The primary paper is pinned to https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18443v3 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.18443v3; paper-v3-pdf-sha256=d006f3f9100afd24e728ab469edd44974c849133121b2a4e53525605b9e44bba. The official code snapshot is https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/tree/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d with tree=3e687331642387eb657ac0ba4f49d8f44e4e748b, README sha256=1383b3f0f5a10cc9a7eebab46e929cddaedf370a80d17b379d21dc380b31ada3, olmocr/bench/benchmark.py sha256=7857eeafeb4bcef911116eb84813fa0a7949d2706c6baf3ee0a9cec706337bc2, olmocr/bench/tests.py sha256=ff36b3cdf81c4a94f3e43cb78de8a31607eb6a0d140d0bfbfb2fe44122b55727, and olmocr/bench/utils.py sha256=dc0b8cde64c9be796e3642094b63f308fd19fe1835396b3340ab4c3a6c9b50f0. The official data snapshot is https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/olmOCR-bench/tree/54a96a6fb6a2bd3b297e59869491db4d3625b711 with tree=bdffef536220c0940b08246883c2e3ebe3e3cb46, README sha256=92ce373a5e384628dc2fa8ef30918d3450c44ca89e89dfaea55c9b80e71fbf44, and eval.yaml sha256=e8438c6c3d2b014e6be5313eb8444a223d26be45d74c3baf33ffab3aa45572ff. The seven fixed JSONL sha256 values are arxiv_math=5c1ba4770168a2312bf248c8b0125ed2279ec9f664ce64ba7cb52e3c41e4987c, headers_footers=315822b0fcd684eab7099bfb162ea45dc2384b23874be9529d60cd85b7e9c274, long_tiny_text=9ebe6a5fa690e78098e088b9eb677c4bb4212ed9b946be80b2d79a1a6c2a0e1a, multi_column=50192fd72f18434f3303b501bc9347763fb4b865238b7636604d3f6ebdf01595, old_scans=0cb14b2a5c3a08383f256931f79d1deea737e2635e0f1766b0fe0377f9416a0d, old_scans_math=aa514fb0c4c06aa077cadf316c2aede9716f62088ea1011683e059f7be67a8bd, and table_tests=e37a99bd60de56c62cd3f4c1b7910b603641901c15ae119f849ffefa86cde120. Paper Section 3 defines the benchmark as deterministic pass or fail unit tests on a page output. It intentionally avoids an LLM judge and avoids fuzzy whole-reference metrics such as edit distance or ROUGE, while individual text facts may use bounded fuzzy matching. It says documents that both contain personally identifiable information and are not meant for public dissemination are removed, reusing the olmOCR-mix-0225 PII prompt, and benchmark PDF URLs are deduplicated against olmOCR-mix-0225. The graph preserves the conjunction in the paper sentence and does not silently strengthen it to two independent exclusion filters. Paper Section 3.2 says test creation combines manual design and review with GPT-4o prompting, and Appendix F.2 says prompt executions typically use sampling temperature 0.1. The paper constructs seven document sources. arXiv Math has 522 PDFs and 2,927 formula tests from recent math papers with one TeX source and a rendered PDF; olmOCR identifies candidate pages, dynamic programming aligns them to source, KaTeX compatibility is checked, and humans remove custom-macro mismatches and split multipart equations. Old Scans Math has 36 public-domain Internet Archive textbook PDFs and 458 formula tests, using random pages, olmOCR candidate discovery, and manual formula annotation. Tables has 188 PDFs and 1,020 relationship tests from the internal crawl used for the training mix; Gemini Flash 2.0 filters table pages and proposes relationships between random cells, followed by manual review. Old Scans has 98 Library of Congress PDFs and 526 tests: scripts derive natural reading-order pairs from human transcriptions, humans add header and footer absence tests, and all cases receive a second review. Headers Footers has 266 internal-crawl PDFs and 753 absence tests: DocLayout-YOLO finds abandon regions, the remaining page is masked, Gemini Flash 2.0 extracts peripheral text, and reviewers correct snippets and first-N or last-N conditions. Multi Column has 231 internal-crawl PDFs and 884 reading-order tests: pages are visually sampled, Claude Sonnet 3.7 renders HTML, simple coherent before and after spans are extracted while avoiding math and scripts, and every entry is reviewed. Long Tiny Text has 62 dense Internet Archive PDFs and 442 presence tests generated with Gemini Flash 2.0 and manually verified. Paper-v3 Table 3 and Appendix Table 10 define 7,010 core tests: 721 text presence, 823 text absence, 1,061 natural reading order, 1,020 table accuracy, and 3,385 math formula accuracy. The seven source row counts are 2,927, 458, 1,020, 526, 753, 884, and 442 and sum to 7,010. Table 10 reports 1,403 PDFs, while one Section 3 prose sentence still says 1,402 distinct PDFs and the conclusion says 1,403. The diagrams preserve this paper-internal count boundary and use the table and fixed release total without deleting the conflicting prose fact. The fixed HF tree contains exactly 1,403 PDF LFS paths and seven JSONL files. Parsing the fixed JSONL yields exactly 7,019 physical records and 1,403 unique PDF references. Of those records, 7,010 are the five paper core types with the exact published distribution; nine are explicit baseline entries, seven in headers_footers and two in table_tests, that disable disallowed-character checks for legitimate pages. The pinned evaluator adds a default baseline to every PDF lacking one, so a full run has one baseline per 1,403 PDFs rather than treating nine as the entire baseline set. The release README continues to call the benchmark 7,010 unit tests because that headline counts the paper core facts, not the runtime baseline group. For text comparisons, paper and code normalize br tags, whitespace, Markdown bold and italics, Unicode quotes and hyphens, and Unicode NFC. Text presence and absence allow fuzzy matching and optional first-N or last-N windows; presence is case-sensitive by default and absence is not. Reading order requires a fuzzy-matched before span to occur before an after span. Table tests parse Markdown and HTML and validate target cell neighbors, while complex row or column spans require HTML. Formula tests render reference and candidate LaTeX with KaTeX and compare rendered symbols and relative bounding boxes. Every PDF receives a baseline requiring alphanumeric output, rejecting ending n-gram loops with a count greater than 30, and rejecting unexpected Chinese, Japanese, or emoji characters unless an explicit baseline disables that check. Each fact produces a binary result. Paper Section 3.3 computes a percentage for each of the seven document sources plus the default baseline source, then takes the equal mean of those eight percentages. This is a macro-average over source groups, not a micro-average over the 7,010 unevenly distributed core facts. Paper Table 4 reports 95 percent confidence intervals from 10,000 bootstrap samples. The pinned current evaluator is later than the paper protocol. It supports repeated Markdown generations, reduces each fact to pass when more than half the repeats pass, adds format and footnote test classes not present in the paper five-class release, and defaults to 1,000 bootstrap samples rather than the paper Table 4 value of 10,000. At this revision, the nine explicit baselines keep their source JSONL mapping, while only synthesized defaults enter the separate baseline group; it then averages seven JSONL group rates plus that baseline group. Its bootstrap resamples within the supplied group splits, a detail not stated by the paper. The diagrams place these differences in a dashed later-evaluator boundary so they cannot rewrite the paper construction or fixed five-class data release. The fixed HF revision was last updated in 2026 for eval.yaml integration and is used as an immutable audit snapshot, not evidence that every later repository feature existed in the 2025 paper. The paper names GPT-4o, Gemini Flash 2.0, Claude Sonnet 3.7, and DocLayout-YOLO, and prints several prompts, but it does not disclose immutable API checkpoints, all generation seeds, the identity of the internal PDF repository, exact source sampling seeds, every rejected candidate, or a complete frozen construction environment. Current miner scripts are useful implementation evidence but are not treated as proof that the original release can be reconstructed byte for byte. The fixed dataset uses ODC-BY-1.0 and preserves per-record source URLs, while original PDFs retain their upstream provenance and rights. The diagrams therefore do not claim that ODC-BY transfers ownership of source documents, do not invent public replacements for internal corpora, and do not fold later format or footnote tests into the paper benchmark.
